subject: ESS HL
title: Valora Metropolitan Fringe: Atmosphere, Climate and Ecosystem Recovery
summary: A fictional metropolitan fringe used to investigate climate and biomes, ecological succession, atmospheric processes, stratospheric ozone, air quality and integrated environmental management. All names and data are hypothetical and created for examination practice.
requiredUnits: 2.5 Zonation, succession and change in ecosystems

resources.title: Resource 1: Regional background
resources.text: Valora is a rapidly expanding city beside a seasonally dry woodland. A severe wildfire burned 6,400 ha of woodland in 2022. The city also experiences winter air-pollution episodes when cool, still conditions trap pollutants near the surface. A national atmospheric observatory 40 km away monitors total-column stratospheric ozone. The regional government is considering woodland restoration, tighter vehicle-emission controls, improved refrigerant recovery and limits on new development at the urban fringe.

resources.title: Resource 2: Climate data for Valora
resources.description: Long-term monthly means for four representative months.
resources.note: Most annual rainfall occurs from late autumn to early spring; summers are hot and dry.

resources.title: Resource 3: Post-fire recovery
resources.description: Measurements from permanent plots in the burned woodland.
columns: Mean plant species richness per plot
resources.note: Unburned reference plots average 88% vegetation cover, 25 species per plot and a soil-carbon index of 110.

resources.title: Resource 4: Winter atmosphere and PM2.5
resources.description: Mean observations during five winter monitoring days.
resources.note: A lower mixing layer and weaker winds reduce vertical and horizontal dispersion of pollutants.

resources.title: Resource 5: Ozone-layer indicators
resources.description: Hypothetical monitoring data for the wider region.
resources.note: Lower values of the consumption index indicate reduced use of controlled ozone-depleting substances.

resources.title: Resource 6: Stakeholder positions
resources.text: Conservation groups support assisted woodland regeneration and restrictions on urban expansion near recovering habitat. Property developers argue that housing demand requires some fringe development. Public-health groups support stricter vehicle-emission rules during winter. Appliance and cooling businesses support refrigerant recovery but request financial support for equipment and technician training. The national government is party to an international agreement controlling ozone-depleting substances and requires recovery of specified refrigerants from large commercial systems.
